To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have conducted a search of the GC region for pulsars using a new, low-frequency radio data set.

(1) we conducted a search for radio pulsars toward the GC at a low frequency in order to take maximum advantage of the very low radio flux densities of pulsars; (2) we found no pulsar candidates, but we did find seven steep-spectrum sources that are potential pulsar candidates; (3) we conducted a follow-up search with the GBT and found no pulsations from the candidates; and (4) we estimated the distances to the candidates using two different models,
We have conducted a sensitive search for steep-spectrum pulsar candidates in the direction of the Galactic Center using low-frequency radio data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for new pulsars in the direction of the Galactic Centre.
pulsar searches in the Galactic plane.
the search for pulsars in the GC region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GC region does not contain any pulsars with periods shorter than ∼0.5 s and distances less than ∼8 kps.
we have not found any new pulsar candidates in the GC region.
the GC pulsar population is likely to be composed of a large population of MSPs with periods of ∼10-100 ms and distances of ∼4-8 kpc.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found no evidence for MSPs at distances greater than ∼3 kpc toward the GC.
a large fraction of the GC pulsar population is likely to be located within ∼4.3 kpc of the GC.
the nondetections of pulsations in the GC region are not inconsistent with the hypothesis that the excess gamma-ray emission is due to a population of ∼1000 MSPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a population of MSPs is unlikely to be the source of the gamma-ray excess, and the excess is more likely due to unresolved sources of nonthermal emission.
the GC is not an efficient region for pulsar searches, even at low frequencies, and that the GC region will remain an extremely challenging environment to detect pulsars.
, while our search has not yielded new pulsar candidates, it has demonstrated that the GC region is a challenging place for pulsar detection and has provided a useful baseline for future searches.
